title: Topic 9: Numbers, Prices & Money - Vocabulary
description: Core words for numbers, prices & money: money, price, dollar, cent, cheap, expensive, buy, pay. 8 tap exercises with embedded grammar.
canDoStatement: Count, understand prices, handle money situations
introductionText:
money = dollars and cents!  |  price = 90 dollars is a price
dollar = 1.00  |  cent = 0.01 (100 cents = 1 dollar)
cheap = a small price :)  |  expensive = a big price!
buy = get a thing with money  |  pay = give the money
+ set: numbers 13-100 with audio; danger pairs 13/30,
14/40, 15/50 flagged
+ phrase bank: How much is it? | How much are they? |
That is expensive!

grammarBlocks.title: HOW MUCH IS / HOW MUCH ARE (singular vs plural - extends the
grammarBlocks.explanation: HOW MUCH IS / HOW MUCH ARE (singular vs plural - extends the T6 is/are agreement work) + plural -s recycling (G3). Numbers 13-100 taught as a SET on the intro card (precedent: T2 alphabet, T8 days).
patterns: How much IS + singular / How much ARE + plural

questions.question: The table is 500 dollars! It is very ___.
Tap the missing word: I want this book. I ___ it with my money.
Tap the missing word: The price is ten dollars. I ___ with my card.
A: How much is the chair? B: ___
Grammar: How much ___ the bed? How much ___ the chairs?
Grammar: One chair is cheap. Four ___ are expensive!

explanations.A1-T09-VOC-Q2: Expensive = a big price. Cheap = a small price.
explanations.A1-T09-VOC-Q3: Buy = get a thing with money.
explanations.A1-T09-VOC-Q5: thirTEEN = 13. thirTY = 30. Listen for the end!
explanations.A1-T09-VOC-Q6: How much...? asks the PRICE -> answer in dollars.
explanations.A1-T09-VOC-Q7: One bed -> IS. Two or more chairs -> ARE.
